description: An industry where an uneventful career is the mark of excellence, which makes it hard to interview. Ask about restoration, permitting, and the specific engineering rather than making the guest a proxy for climate politics.

questions.text: Walk me through a storm restoration from the moment the lights go out.
questions.lands_because: Mutual aid, crew logistics, prioritization, and public pressure all in one operational story. It is the most vivid material this industry has.
followups: How do you decide whose power comes back first?

questions.text: How much of a project is engineering, and how much is permitting and interconnection?
questions.lands_because: Permitting and interconnection queues dominate project timelines and are invisible to the public. Naming them proves you know where the bottleneck actually is.
followups: What would it take to shorten that?

questions.text: What does the public misunderstand about how the grid actually stays balanced?
questions.lands_because: Grid operators genuinely enjoy explaining this, and second-by-second balancing is a great piece of audience education.
followups: What is the scariest hour you have watched on the board?

questions.text: You cannot simply build what you think is best - who has to approve it, and how does that change the engineering?
questions.lands_because: Acknowledges regulatory constraint up front, which frees the guest to describe how rate cases and commissions actually shape technical decisions.
followups: What would you build if the constraint disappeared?

questions.text: In a field where success is nothing happening, how do you know when you have done well?
questions.lands_because: Names the central psychological oddity of reliability work. It is a distinctive question that yields something genuinely reflective.

questions.text: What does the energy transition look like from inside operations, as opposed to from a conference stage?
questions.lands_because: Invites the operational reality - interconnection, materials, workforce, dispatchability - without asking the guest to take a political position.
followups: What is harder than people think? What is easier?
